principle: Corrections are recorded additively. No frozen run directory, receipt or native record was edited.

items.claim: protocol/arm-budgets/deepseek41.json carries a stale selector label deepseek-v4-flash while all 470 receipts record opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash
items.finding: Confirmed as a label, but it is not a per-arm field. The only occurrence is bound.deepseek_metadata.selector, which is the frozen continuation-3 cost policy block describing the HYBRID arm's research model (opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash). Every arm's budget copies the whole cost policy into `bound`, so every continuation-4 arm carries it, including the claude arms.

evidence.native_usage_rows: 470 of 470 rows across jobs/*/raw-omp/usage.json record provider opencode-go, model deepseek-v4.1-flash

items.correction: cost_policy.json renames the legacy block to hybrid_arm_deepseek_metadata and states what it applies to; cost_policy.json already carries the correct per-arm selectors under continuation4_arms. The rename is a protocol change and lands at the next idle window with a new freeze hash. Arm budgets already written keep their bytes; this record is the correction of the label for the bundle.

items.claim: the oh-my-pi runtime is the omp-18.1.12-linux-x64 binary self-reporting omp/18.2.2, not 18.1.13
items.finding: Confirmed, with a date boundary. ~/.local/bin/omp is a symlink to /mnt/Cursor/PM-Experiments/omp-runtimes/omp-18.1.12-linux-x64/omp-linux-x64 - a directory name, not a version. That binary self-reported omp/18.1.13 (sha 3be5a308cc91e6f6bba148175fbe651d3583ff6d32ae221cb931dc08a64e1f39) when the union attempt ran at 18:49Z, and self-reports omp/18.2.2 (sha 77c3520ab8ef8318dda02a0715e3b6e69589c427dc23f90a4bb97650caa72f72) since Jared updated it in place; both deepseek41 attempts ran against 18.2.2.
items.correction: arm-outputs/runtime-identity.json records invoked path, resolved binary, self-reported version and sha256 both as installed now and as each arm's own job records report them; the per-arm rows are authoritative because each job hashes the binary it actually ran. The adapters' hardcoded verified_runtime_version becomes a live reading (version plus binary hash) at the next idle window, so a runtime that changes between the gate and the campaign fails closed instead of being recorded falsely.
items.effect_on_results: none; no arm ran against a runtime other than the one its own job records name

items.question: is 41 responses on a 40 ceiling the pre-fix counting or a remaining off-by-one in record_response
items.answer: Neither: it is the kill window of a post-response boundary, and the accounting is consistent.

evidence.journal_sequence_J0018: response_recorded ... next_request_denied(model_request_limit) -> response_recorded 0.2 s later -> next_request_denied -> job_end_accounting
evidence.post_fix_consistency: durable request_count 41 equals receipts 41 in that job, and every one of the 12 jobs reconciled with 0 unresolved
evidence.pre_fix_contrast: in attempt 1 the same shape produced receipts 41 against a durable count of 40, which failed reconciliation; that was the defect record_response fixed

items.meaning: The ceiling is enforced after a response, so oh-my-pi can already have dispatched one more request before the adapter kills it. The limit should be read as "at most 40 admitted responses, with at most one further response already in flight", not as a hard 40.
items.cost_effect: immaterial here: the arm captured $0.5315 against a $50 cap

items.defect: The Claude Code CLI emits one assistant event per content block, with the same message id repeated up to five times. The adapter counted events as model responses, so a 40-response ceiling fired at about 17 real responses and every job died in ~2 minutes. The sidecar request count was inflated the same way, and the durable Meter count stayed 0 because the adapter never called the boundary, so each job reconciled as incomplete and carried a $12 cold liability.

evidence.shape: attempt-1 jobs stop at exactly 40 assistant events with 10-22 distinct message ids (J0017: 40 events, 17 ids)

items.fix: Count distinct response ids, record one usage row per response, and drive the durable Meter per response. Verified by replaying the archived stream: 17 requests, collector complete, zero gaps.
items.effect_on_scored_results: none; the spoiled attempt is archived and not scored

items.defect: request_boundary refuses to register a request once a ceiling is hit, but the response that triggered the denial had already happened and carried a receipt. Job-end receipts therefore exceeded the durable request count by one, reconciliation demands equality, and each failed job retained a $12 liability until the arm cap denied further admissions.

evidence.shape: six jobs with receipts = durable count + 1, each reconciled false, $72.00 of phantom liability against a $50 cap, arm ended Stop: insufficient_priced_usage_headroom

items.fix: cost_watch.record_response always registers a response that already happened and only denies the next request; a ceiling denial no longer rewrites the runtime status, only a monetary stop does.
items.effect_on_scored_results: none; the rerun under the fixed freeze reconciled 12 of 12

items.defect: discovery_to_plan.put() wrote through a fixed temp name, <name>.tmp, while bounded_campaign writes jobs/<job>/worker-process.json from two places at once: the campaign parent about ten times a second and the worker child once at startup. One renamed the other's temp file away and the loser's rename raised FileNotFoundError, which is not a Stop, so the campaign ended as a workflow_error.

evidence.shape: both campaign-terminal.json files record the identical worker-process.json.tmp FileNotFoundError, 26.74 s apart, each naming its own run directory
evidence.consequence: the four sub-second interrupted jobs were cancelled by the crash's own shutdown path, not by anything of their own

items.fix: put() writes to a temp name unique to the writing process and call and removes its own temp file on failure. Regression test protocol/test_worker_record_races.py runs two stub campaigns concurrently and also asserts that the old shared name still loses the rename.
items.effect_on_scored_results: none; both arms were rerun from scratch under the fixed freeze

items.defect: Both adapters declared a hardcoded verified_runtime_version while oh-my-pi was updated in place at the same path during the session (omp/18.1.13 -> omp/18.2.2), so the declared version could be false while every job record was right.

evidence.per_run_identities: runtime-identity.json, regenerated from all eleven runs

items.fix: omp_native.installed_runtime() and the Claude equivalent shell --version and hash the binary at capability time; gates record the runtime block and the boundary check compares the binary hash, so a runtime that changes between gate and campaign fails closed.
items.effect_on_scored_results: none; no arm ran against a runtime other than the one its own job records name

scope: C1-C3 are the adjudicator bookkeeping items. D1-D4 are the four defects found while the arms ran; each has the attempt it spoiled archived rather than scored, and each was fixed in a freeze that later arms ran under.
